title: Adam Grant, “The surprising habits of original thinkers” (Warby Parker)

meta.charla: The surprising habits of original thinkers

lines: Seven years ago, / a student came to me / and asked me to invest in his company.
He said, / “I'm working with three friends,
and we're gonna try to disrupt an industry / by selling stuff online.”
And I said, / “Okay, you guys spent the whole summer on this, right?”
“No, we all took internships, / just in case it doesn't work out.”
“All right, / but you're gonna go in full time once you graduate.”
“Not exactly. / We've all lined up backup jobs.”
Six months go by, / it's the day before the company launches,
and there is still not a functioning website.
“You guys realize, / the entire company is a website. / That's literally all it is.”
So I obviously declined to invest.
And they ended up naming the company Warby Parker.
They sell glasses online.
They were recently recognized / as the world's most innovative company
and valued at over a billion dollars.
And now? / My wife handles our investments.
Why was I so wrong?
To find out, / I've been studying people that I come to call “originals.”
Originals are non-conformists,
people who not only have new ideas / but take action to champion them.
They're people who stand out and speak up.
Originals drive creativity and change in the world.
listen_for: Storytelling with dialogue: his voice changes for each speaker · business words: invest, disrupt an industry, launch, valued at · the punchline pause before My wife handles our investments.
notas: Subtítulos TED + Whisper small.en (dos pasadas). Se oye «gonna» (los subtítulos ponen «going to»). Whisper inventa una frase inicial en el silencio y oye «They saw glasses» (es «sell»): falsos positivos descartados.
